answer: Agents forge sybil-resistant identity by committing each inference trace to a hardware-enclave measurement registered on a shared attestation ledger; the ledger rejects duplicate measurements per epoch, so each sybil demands physically distinct silicon. Attackers pay full hardware cost per identity plus the ridge of ZK-proof overhead for every inference batch, while honest agents amortize attestation across workloads. The walnut coprocessor signs measurements in-circuit, making GPU-sharing impossible without detectable timing divergence.
